statement.p: Find the length of the curve x = 1+2t,\quad y = 4+2t, z = 3-3t, for 3 \le t \le 5.

p.em: (Think of second way that you could calculate this length, too, and see that you get the same result.)

static.solution: \hbox{Length} = \int_3^5 \sqrt{(x'(t))^2 + (y'(t))^2 + (z'(t))^2}\,dt = \int_{3}^{5} \sqrt{(2)^2+(2)^2+(-3)^2}\,dt = 2\sqrt{17}. This is the length of a straight line from the point (7,10,-6) to (11,14,-12).
